title: Cassandra Practice
description: Practise the twelve ideas in this Cassandra course. Choose an answer, then read why it fits the example.

exercises.question: How many replicas does this practice setup request?
exercises.explanation: A keyspace groups Cassandra tables and defines replication. Replication means how many copies of data are kept across nodes.

exercises.question: Which field is the partition key?
exercises.explanation: The partition key chooses a group of rows stored together. A clustering column orders rows inside that partition.

exercises.question: What identifies this row uniquely?
exercises.explanation: An INSERT writes values at a primary-key address. Writing the same key again updates those supplied values rather than making a duplicate row.

exercises.question: Which condition lets this query choose a partition?
exercises.explanation: A Cassandra query is efficient when it names the partition key. It can then read the rows grouped under that key.

exercises.question: What column supplies this range?
exercises.explanation: After choosing a partition, a query can use a range on its clustering column. This is useful for a reader's recent days.

exercises.question: Why add month to this partition key?
options: To sort all readers alphabetically on one node
To split an unbounded history into smaller groups
exercises.explanation: A partition should not grow without a useful bound. A time bucket can split a long history into smaller groups.

exercises.question: What unit is USING TTL 60 measured in?
exercises.explanation: A TTL gives written values a time to live. Cassandra removes them from ordinary reads after they expire.

exercises.question: Why include both key parts in the WHERE clause?
options: To make a title become a primary key
To identify the exact row to update
exercises.explanation: An UPDATE names the row through its key and changes selected values. Cassandra writes can create missing non-key values at that address.

exercises.question: What is a tombstone used for?
exercises.explanation: A DELETE marks selected data as deleted. Cassandra uses tombstones so replicas can learn that a value was removed.

exercises.question: Is a large unrelated batch automatically faster?
options: Yes, more partitions always make it faster
No, it can add coordination cost
exercises.explanation: A batch can group related mutations. It is not a general speed trick for sending many unrelated partitions at once.

exercises.question: Does repeating this counter update leave the value unchanged?
options: Yes, every counter update is idempotent
exercises.explanation: Cassandra counters use a special column type and update rules. Keep them in a table designed for counts.

exercises.question: How many responses form a quorum of three?
exercises.explanation: A consistency level tells Cassandra how many replicas must answer an operation. It only makes sense together with the replication setup.
